findings.title: Shared TLS context can leak client certificates across requests
findings.suggested_fix: Use an isolated SSLContext for requests with client certificates so loading one cert cannot affect later handshakes.

testing_gaps: No regression test covers requests with distinct or absent client certificates sharing the verify=True context across destinations or concurrent handshakes.

residual_risks: Existing TLS tests exercise rejection with verify=True and success with verify=False or an explicit CA bundle, but do not show a successful handshake through the newly preloaded default trust context.
testing_gaps: Add an offline TLS integration test where a server certificate chains to a CA in DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH and verify=True succeeds.
Add a CA directory verification test; the changed request-context branch now selects ca_cert_dir when verify is a directory, but current custom-CA success coverage uses a bundle file.
Exercise client certificate authentication with verify=True and the preloaded context; current mTLS coverage passes cert together with verify=False.
